tools.title: Official Unreal MCP
tools.summary: Epic's native MCP server and Toolset Registry bridge. This should be the primary AI transport layer for UE 5.8+.
why: AICallable tool discovery through Toolset Registry
Works with MCP-compatible agents such as Codex
workflow: Start the MCP server from Unreal Editor.
Connect Codex using the generated MCP configuration.
Prefer tool calls over UI automation when a native tool exists.
tools.codex: Foundation layer. Our plugin should extend it rather than create a parallel protocol server.
tools.caution: Experimental API surface can change between engine versions; pin the supported Unreal version and verify tool discovery after upgrades.

tools.title: Unreal MCP Tools (this repository)
tools.summary: Our production-oriented extension layer for Blueprint inspection, graph mutation, validation and Codex workflows.
workflow: Install Plugin/UnrealMCPTools into the game project.
Compile, validate, re-read, then explicitly save.
tools.codex: Primary custom toolset layer. Add project-specific tools here only when Epic does not already expose them.
tools.caution: Must be built with UHT/UBT in a real UE 5.8 editor target before being treated as verified.

tools.title: Slate Inspector Toolset
tools.summary: Playwright-style automation for Unreal Editor Slate UI: snapshots, screenshots, clicks, typing, drag, wait and form filling.
why: Lets Codex operate editor UI when no native API exists
Useful for editor plugins and custom tools
workflow: Take a screenshot when visual evidence matters.
tools.codex: Fallback lane after native MCP/API tools. Excellent for UMG/editor workflow smoke tests.
tools.caution: Do not use UI automation when a deterministic native tool exists; UI labels and layouts are more fragile.

tools.title: Automation Test MCP Toolset
tools.summary: Epic MCP toolset that discovers, runs, stops and retrieves Unreal Automation Framework test results.
why: Codex can execute real Unreal tests
tools.codex: Use as the standard post-change verification lane for editor/gameplay code and content tests.
tools.caution: Discovery is asynchronous and can take time; do not repeatedly rediscover unless tests changed.

tools.title: Live Coding MCP Toolset
tools.summary: Triggers Unreal Live Coding compilation and returns compiler diagnostics directly to MCP clients.
workflow: Enable Live Coding in Editor Preferences.
Use a full editor rebuild when reflection/layout changes require it.
tools.codex: Use for short compile/fix loops; pair with AutomationTestToolset after successful compilation.
tools.caution: Live Coding is not a substitute for a clean UBT/UHT rebuild after UCLASS/USTRUCT/UFUNCTION signature or module-level changes.

tools.title: Python Editor Scripting
tools.summary: Unreal's embedded Python lane for asset processing, editor automation and pipeline integration.
workflow: Enable Python Editor Script Plugin and Editor Scripting Utilities.
Use Python for bulk deterministic operations.
Promote stable critical behavior to C++ when stronger typing/API coverage is required.
tools.codex: Good implementation lane for generated one-off or project pipeline scripts, especially content operations.
tools.caution: Python API coverage differs from C++; do not force graph authoring through Python when editor C++ APIs are more reliable.

tools.title: Editor Utility Widgets
tools.summary: Dockable UMG-based editor tools for project-specific buttons, dashboards and workflows.
why: Can wrap repetitive project actions in a friendly UI
workflow: Keep runtime and editor responsibilities separate.
Use MCP or Slate Inspector to drive it when agent automation is useful.
tools.codex: Codex can create/support EUWs and later drive them through Slate Inspector when a direct tool call is not available.
tools.caution: Do not hide important business logic only inside UI graphs; keep reusable logic in functions/subsystems/libraries.

tools.title: Scriptable Tools System
tools.summary: Blueprint-accessible Interactive Tools Framework for building custom viewport interaction tools and editor modes.
workflow: Create an editor-only Scriptable Tool Blueprint.
tools.codex: Useful when the optimal workflow needs a human-in-the-loop viewport tool rather than a hidden command.
tools.caution: This is for editor tooling, not runtime gameplay.

tools.title: ZiggyMar / unreal-mcp
tools.summary: Community Unreal MCP bridge with Blueprint graph editing, project indexing and node catalog ideas worth studying.
workflow: Port only the ideas/API patterns we need.
Prefer Epic's official MCP transport on UE 5.8.
tools.codex: Architecture reference for deeper graph tooling and project indexing.
tools.caution: Third-party implementation; do not couple our production path to it when the official MCP layer covers transport.

tools.title: SunGrow Blueprint Extractor
tools.summary: Blueprint and StateTree extraction/authoring system with a large machine-friendly MCP contract.
why: Useful design ideas for read/verify/save workflows
workflow: Study its resource schemas and extraction model.
Port features only after checking UE 5.8 APIs.
tools.codex: Reference for richer asset/resource representations and StateTree support.
tools.caution: Treat compatibility and validation claims as repository-specific; verify against the target editor build.

tools.title: UnrealAIAssistant
tools.summary: Editor-integrated AI panel supporting Codex/Claude plus MCP tools for assets, Blueprints, materials, characters and viewport capture.
workflow: Study the editor panel and task orchestration UX.
Do not vendor blindly because its documented baseline is UE 5.5.
Port useful concepts into our 5.8-native layer.
tools.codex: Reference for an optional dockable assistant experience inside Unreal.
tools.caution: Version baseline differs from ours; editor APIs may need migration.

tools.title: UE Node2Code
tools.summary: Exports Material and Niagara node graphs into compact text that is easier for AI agents to reason about.
why: Useful when our native graph readers do not cover a graph type
workflow: Install as a project plugin if compatible.
Feed compact text to Codex for analysis.
Apply edits through Unreal-native APIs/editor tools.
tools.codex: Useful read-only bridge for graph types beyond standard Blueprints.
tools.caution: Prefer native structured readers once our MCP plugin supports the same graph type.

tools.title: UAssetAPI
tools.summary: Low-level .NET library for reading and writing Unreal assets outside the editor.
why: Useful for forensic or pipeline tasks when Unreal Editor is unavailable
workflow: Keep production Blueprint semantic writes inside Unreal Editor.
Pin the Unreal asset version before parsing/writing.
Validate any generated assets by opening them in Unreal.
tools.codex: Fallback offline asset-inspection lane, not the normal production mutation path.
tools.caution: Direct binary asset writes bypass Unreal editor invariants and compilation; use with strict safeguards.

tools.title: PCG MCP Toolset
tools.summary: Epic toolset that lets an AI assistant build and modify PCG graphs using AICallable Unreal-native operations.
why: Creates and edits PCG graph nodes through Unreal APIs
Exposes graph structure and node schemas to agents
Pairs naturally with the official Unreal MCP server
workflow: Enable PCG, PCGToolset, ToolsetRegistry and ModelContextProtocol.
Ask the agent to inspect the graph before modification.
Use native PCG tool calls to add nodes/subgraphs and parameters.
Execute/validate the graph and inspect generated output before saving.
tools.codex: Prefer this official toolset over adding duplicate PCG mutation methods to UnrealMCPTools.
tools.caution: The PCGToolset plugin is Experimental in UE 5.8. Pin the engine version and smoke-test tool contracts after upgrades.

tools.title: Blueprint Assist
tools.summary: Automatic Blueprint graph formatting plus keyboard-first node navigation and editing.
workflow: Share team settings through source control.
Format after meaningful graph changes, not on every tiny operation.
Use it as presentation/readability tooling, not architecture.
tools.codex: After Codex mutates a graph, a formatter integration could normalize node layout before review.
tools.caution: Formatting cannot fix bad responsibilities or coupling. Keep architecture rules separate.

tools.title: Auto Size Comments
tools.summary: Automatically keeps Blueprint comment boxes sized around their nodes and supports comment style presets.
workflow: Install into the project/engine plugin folder.
Group logic by responsibility, not by arbitrary screen region.
tools.codex: Codex can preserve comments and create meaningful graph sections; this plugin keeps the visual grouping tidy.
tools.caution: Some graph types have compatibility limitations; verify on the target UE version.

tools.title: Electronic Nodes
tools.summary: Alternative wire rendering for Blueprint, Material and other graph editors.
workflow: Install only if a UE 5.8-compatible build is available.
Do not make screenshots/reviews depend on personal-only styling.
tools.codex: No direct automation value; improves human review of graphs generated or edited by Codex.
tools.caution: The public compatibility table currently documents up to UE 5.7; verify before adopting on 5.8.

tools.title: Blueprint Diff
tools.summary: Unreal's asset-aware diff workflow for comparing Blueprint revisions instead of treating .uasset files as opaque binaries.
workflow: Compare the working Blueprint against the previous revision.
Review graph, defaults and component changes.
Capture diff evidence in PRs for important assets.
tools.codex: Use as a human/automation verification concept: re-read changed graphs and surface a semantic summary before commit.
tools.caution: Git textual diff is not meaningful for .uasset files; use Unreal-aware diffing.

tools.title: BlueprintUE
tools.summary: Plugin/service workflow for sharing Blueprint graphs in a web-readable format.
why: Good for bug reports and design review
workflow: Keep source-of-truth in the Unreal project.
Do not upload proprietary logic without approval.
tools.codex: Useful for sharing a graph snapshot with humans; not required for internal MCP editing.
tools.caution: External service and documented plugin compatibility must be reviewed before project use.

tools.title: RyHelpfulHelpers
tools.summary: Large helper plugin exposing runtime/editor utilities for Blueprints and C++.
workflow: Audit only the helpers you would actually use.
Avoid taking a large dependency for one trivial helper.
Wrap adopted helpers behind project abstractions if they become core.
tools.codex: Reference source for missing utility functions; can reduce generated boilerplate.
tools.caution: Broad helper libraries can become dependency magnets; evaluate footprint and ownership.

tools.title: Blueprint Console Commands
tools.summary: Makes it easy to expose Blueprint functions as developer console/cheat commands.
workflow: Use commands to reproduce states quickly.
Pair with automation tests where a scenario becomes stable.
tools.codex: Codex can call documented console commands during PIE debugging or generate new debug-only commands.
tools.caution: Never expose privileged/debug commands in shipping builds unintentionally.

tools.title: Quick Actions
tools.summary: Open-source Unreal editor productivity plugin from Out-of-the-Box Plugins.
why: Good source of reusable editor extension patterns
Potential replacement for one-off repetitive editor actions
workflow: Review current feature list against your workflow.
Adopt only actions that save repeated manual work.
Keep project-critical automation in our own toolset or official APIs.
tools.codex: Potential human productivity companion; source also provides editor-extension implementation examples.
tools.caution: Treat as optional convenience, not a required project dependency.

tools.title: FlowGraph
tools.summary: Design-agnostic async node graph for game flow, quests, sequences and narrative scripting.
workflow: Use when the game has substantial quest/narrative/event flow.
Use FlowGraph to orchestrate, not own every gameplay detail.
tools.codex: Codex can help author custom flow nodes and inspect flow assets once we expose dedicated readers.
tools.caution: Adds a major architectural abstraction; adopt intentionally, not for tiny projects.

tools.title: Blueprint Header View
tools.summary: Previews a Blueprint class or struct as C++-style declarations for variables, functions, components and dispatchers.
why: Makes Blueprint structure easier to understand from code-oriented workflows
Useful context for Codex before creating equivalent C++ types
Highlights class shape without manually reading every graph
workflow: Right-click a Blueprint class or struct.
Review variables, functions, components and event dispatchers.
Use the preview as migration/design context; implement actual function logic manually in C++.
tools.codex: Use as supporting evidence when deciding whether a Blueprint should remain visual scripting or move behind a C++ API.
tools.caution: This produces declarations, not a complete automatic Blueprint-to-C++ conversion.

tools.title: JetBrains Rider + UnrealLink / RiderLink
tools.summary: Deep Rider/Unreal Editor integration with Blueprint awareness, code navigation, game launch control and enhanced Unreal logs.
why: Navigate from C++ to the corresponding Blueprint in Unreal Editor
Run multiplayer configurations from the IDE
Use Unreal-aware inspections/refactors and filtered editor logs
workflow: Install/open the project in JetBrains Rider.
Install RiderLink into the game or engine when prompted.
Use Find Usages to include Blueprint-derived/reference information.
Launch PIE/server/client configurations and inspect Unreal logs directly from Rider.
tools.codex: Useful companion IDE when Codex edits C++; it provides human verification of reflection usage and Blueprint/C++ coupling.
tools.caution: Rider is a separate commercial IDE depending on your license; RiderLink should match the Rider/engine setup.

tools.title: UnrealXistTools
tools.summary: Cross-platform PowerShell 7 helpers for Unreal project discovery, UAT, clean builds, project files, IDE launch and project refactors.
why: Wraps verbose Unreal command lines in repeatable scripts
Works on Windows, macOS and Linux for many commands
workflow: Clone UnrealXistTools and add it to PATH.
Use UAT.ps1 for build-cook-stage flows and UProjectClean.ps1 for deliberate clean rebuilds.
tools.codex: Reference implementation for shell automation. We can borrow patterns or call equivalent project-local scripts rather than make Codex reconstruct UAT flags every time.
tools.caution: Review every cleanup/refactor command before running it on a working project; destructive switches should never be implicit.

tools.title: Data Validation
tools.summary: Built-in validation framework for naming, budgets, dependency rules and project-specific asset constraints.
workflow: Run validation on save and pre-submit.
Make validation failures block merges for critical rules.
tools.codex: After asset changes, run validators and repair failures before saving/committing.
tools.caution: Keep validators deterministic and actionable; avoid noisy warnings that teams learn to ignore.

tools.title: Automation Test Framework
tools.summary: Unreal framework for unit, feature, smoke, content-stress and screenshot-comparison tests.
workflow: Write fast smoke tests for core invariants.
Add content stress tests for compile/load integrity.
Run targeted tests during development and broader suites in CI.
tools.codex: Codex should add or update tests with behavior changes, then execute them through the MCP toolset.
tools.caution: Do not mark slow tests as Smoke; keep test scope and runtime intentional.

tools.title: Functional Testing
tools.summary: Level/gameplay-oriented tests using Unreal's Functional Testing framework.
workflow: Run through Automation Framework/Gauntlet as needed.
tools.codex: Ideal for Blueprint features where pure C++ unit tests cannot capture the behavior.
tools.caution: Avoid giant all-purpose test maps; small targeted maps are easier to debug.

tools.title: Gauntlet Automation Framework
tools.summary: Launches and orchestrates editor, packaged game, server/client and platform test sessions.
workflow: Collect artifacts/logs and fail CI on test failures.
tools.codex: Codex can generate/update Gauntlet scripts and interpret failures after builds.
tools.caution: Functional tests alone cannot validate every multi-instance replication scenario; Gauntlet fills that gap.

tools.title: Screenshot Comparison Testing
tools.summary: Automated image comparison for catching rendering/UI regressions.
workflow: Run screenshot tests in controlled settings.
Review tolerances and intentional updates carefully.
tools.codex: After visual changes, Codex can run the test and surface failing comparisons for human review.
tools.caution: Rendering differences across hardware/drivers can create noise; control the environment.

tools.title: Visual Logger
tools.summary: Time-based debugging tool that records gameplay events, text, locations, shapes and actor state.
why: Reconstructs what happened before a bug
workflow: Inspect the timeline and spatial snapshots.
Convert recurring manual diagnosis into automated assertions where possible.
tools.codex: Codex can add targeted logging instrumentation and reason from exported logs/screenshots.
tools.caution: Log only meaningful state; excessive logging makes sessions hard to read.

tools.title: Gameplay Debugger
tools.summary: In-game overlay/debug categories for AI, navigation, behavior and custom gameplay state.
why: Faster than opening many editor panels
workflow: Add project-specific categories for complex systems.
tools.codex: Codex can add custom debugger categories for systems it builds so future debugging is easier.
tools.caution: Developer-only instrumentation should not become shipping runtime overhead.

tools.title: Unreal Insights
tools.summary: Unreal's trace analysis suite for CPU, frame timing, tasks, loading and subsystem performance.
tools.codex: Provide trace findings to Codex so it optimizes measured hotspots instead of guessing.
tools.caution: Do not optimize from anecdotes; profile representative builds and scenarios.

tools.title: Memory Insights
tools.summary: Allocation/lifetime analysis inside Unreal Insights for memory leaks, growth and expensive allocation patterns.
workflow: Capture memory traces in the problematic scenario.
tools.codex: Codex can analyze summarized allocation hotspots and adjust ownership/loading logic.
tools.caution: Memory traces can be large; capture focused sessions.

tools.title: Networking Insights
tools.summary: Detailed network traffic profiling inside Unreal Insights.
tools.codex: Use as evidence when Codex refactors replicated Blueprints/C++.
tools.caution: Always profile realistic player counts and network conditions.

tools.title: Stat Commands & Console Profiling
tools.summary: Fast first-pass profiling using stat unit, stat game, stat gpu and related console diagnostics.
why: Guides when to open deeper Insights/GPU tools
workflow: Move to Unreal Insights/GPU profiling for deep diagnosis.
tools.codex: Codex can include performance console-command checklists in feature verification.
tools.caution: Stats are snapshots/aggregates; use trace tools for deep causal analysis.

tools.title: Blueprint Debugger
tools.summary: Pauses Blueprint execution in PIE/SIE with breakpoints, watches, call stacks and step controls.
why: Inspect runtime pin and variable values
Step through visual execution instead of guessing
See breakpoints, watches and execution trace in one place
Debug a specific Blueprint instance in PIE
workflow: Select the Blueprint instance in Debug Object.
Place a breakpoint on the suspicious node.
Run PIE/SIE and reproduce the issue.
Inspect watches/pins and step through execution.
Fix the graph, compile, and reproduce again.
tools.codex: Codex should use MCP-readable state/logging when available, while this remains the human runtime truth tool for complex visual execution bugs.
tools.caution: Pin values are only meaningful after the relevant nodes have executed.

tools.title: Reference Viewer
tools.summary: Visualizes asset dependencies and referencers.
workflow: Replace hard references with soft/data-driven relationships where appropriate.
tools.codex: Our MCP project tools should expose the same dependency data in machine-readable form.
tools.caution: A dependency is not automatically a problem; optimize based on ownership/loading goals.

tools.title: Asset Manager & Primary Assets
tools.summary: Framework for explicit asset discovery, loading, bundles, auditing, cooking and chunking.
workflow: Use soft references for loadable content.
Load/unload through Asset Manager rather than ad-hoc global hard references.
tools.codex: Codex should prefer Asset Manager patterns for large inventories, abilities, maps, cosmetics and downloadable content.
tools.caution: Do not introduce Asset Manager complexity for a tiny fixed-content prototype without need.

tools.title: Data Registries
tools.summary: Global read-only data access layer that can combine tables/curves and support caching/async access.
workflow: Use for shared read-only structured gameplay data.
tools.codex: Useful when building scalable item/config/stat catalogs without hard-coding data in Blueprints.
tools.caution: Not a replacement for SaveGame/session state.

tools.title: Asset Metadata
tools.summary: Editor-only key/value metadata attached to Unreal assets for ownership, workflow and pipeline information.
why: Good for AI-generated asset audit tags
workflow: Use it for search/validation, not runtime gameplay.
tools.codex: Tag generated/modified assets with optional workflow metadata for later audits.
tools.caution: Metadata is editor/pipeline data and is not intended as runtime gameplay state.

tools.title: Derived Data Cache (DDC)
tools.summary: Caches derived/cooked representations so shaders and assets do not rebuild unnecessarily.
workflow: Use local DDC for every developer.
Configure a shared cache for teams/build machines.
Monitor misses when iteration becomes unexpectedly slow.
tools.codex: Infrastructure guidance: never commit DDC; diagnose build slowness before changing game code.
tools.caution: DDC is disposable cache, not source-of-truth content.

tools.title: Zen Storage Server
tools.summary: Epic storage/cache service used by modern Unreal workflows including derived-data distribution.
workflow: Adopt when team/build infrastructure justifies it.
tools.codex: Infrastructure layer rather than gameplay tool; Codex can maintain setup scripts/docs.
tools.caution: Adds operational complexity; small solo projects may not benefit.

tools.title: Asset Audit + Size Map
tools.summary: Built-in asset footprint and dependency-size inspection for identifying oversized content and expensive dependency trees.
why: Export Asset Audit data for analysis
Catch package/cook footprint problems before release
workflow: Open Size Map from an asset/folder or Reference Viewer.
Open Audit Assets for detailed asset information.
Prioritize the largest unexpected dependencies and verify again after optimization.
tools.codex: A future MCP wrapper can export audit data to structured JSON/CSV so Codex can rank size regressions automatically.
tools.caution: Editor Size Map is an approximation of asset footprint; packaged/cooked size can differ due to compression and cooking.

tools.title: Virtual Assets
tools.summary: Separates bulky asset payload data from lightweight package metadata so source-control syncs can become much smaller.
why: Can shorten source-control sync time for large projects
workflow: Measure whether source-control payload size is a real bottleneck.
Configure shared DDC/virtualization on a test project first.
Virtualize supported assets and measure sync/editor behavior before team rollout.
tools.codex: Treat as infrastructure configuration, not a per-asset mutation trick. Codex can audit configuration and rollout scripts.
tools.caution: The documented quickstart assumes specific source-control/DDC infrastructure; do not enable blindly for a small Git project.

tools.title: Redirector Cleanup / Fix Up Redirectors
tools.summary: Repairs references left behind when assets are moved or renamed and removes obsolete redirector objects.
why: Can run interactively or through ResavePackages commandlet
Keeps Content folders and automation predictable
workflow: After a controlled asset move/rename, inspect redirectors.
Use Fixup Redirectors in the Content Browser for local work.
For project-wide maintenance, use the ResavePackages commandlet with FixupRedirectors in a clean branch.
Validate references and commit all resulting asset changes together.
tools.codex: Codex may prepare and run a controlled commandlet workflow, but must inspect git status and never mass-resave the project silently.
tools.caution: Project-wide fixup can touch many binary assets. Run on a clean branch/worktree and review the resulting source-control diff.

tools.title: Git LFS + File Locking Workflow
tools.summary: Store .uasset/.umap in Git LFS and lock binary assets that cannot be merged safely.
workflow: Never attempt text merges of binary assets.
tools.codex: Before mutating a binary asset, verify repository cleanliness and lock/ownership policy; never auto-force conflicts.
tools.caution: LFS alone does not prevent merge conflicts; locking discipline matters.

tools.title: Project Borealis UEGitPlugin
tools.summary: Refactored Unreal Git/LFS source-control provider with file locking and status-branch workflow improvements.
workflow: Evaluate on a disposable UE 5.8 project first.
Keep CLI Git as the source-of-truth fallback.
tools.codex: Useful if the team wants editor-native locks, but Codex can operate Git from CLI without requiring this plugin.
tools.caution: Open issues report compatibility/usability problems in newer UE versions; do not make it mandatory until tested on 5.8.

tools.title: Unreal Commandlets in CI
tools.summary: Run validation, resave, cook and other editor operations headlessly through UnrealEditor-Cmd/commandlets.
workflow: Add targeted project commandlets only for deterministic tasks.
tools.codex: Codex should produce CI commands alongside new validators/tools so every guardrail is automatable.
tools.caution: Headless/commandlet execution can differ from interactive editor paths; test both where relevant.

tools.title: BuildGraph
tools.summary: Epic's XML-based build orchestration layer on top of Unreal Automation Tool.
workflow: Keep BuildGraph scripts in source control.
Separate build, test, cook and publish nodes.
tools.codex: Codex can update BuildGraph definitions when project build/test requirements change.
tools.caution: Start simple; do not build an enterprise pipeline before the project needs it.

tools.title: Clean Build / Cook / Package Verification
tools.summary: Regularly validate the project outside the warm developer editor: clean build, cook and package.
tools.codex: A task is not release-ready merely because PIE works; Codex should report clean build/cook/package status separately.
tools.caution: Live Coding success is insufficient evidence for release readiness.

tools.title: Horde
tools.summary: Epic infrastructure for build automation, remote execution, test automation, studio analytics and device farms.
workflow: Start only when project/team scale justifies dedicated infrastructure.
Pilot Horde locally or on a small server.
Connect agents and one build/test stream.
Add auth, observability and resource pools before broader rollout.
tools.codex: Codex can author BuildGraph/Horde config and inspect logs/results, but infrastructure changes should remain reviewed.
tools.caution: Horde is powerful and operationally heavier than a simple Azure/GitHub pipeline; do not adopt merely because it exists.

tools.title: Unreal Build Accelerator (UBA)
tools.summary: Accelerates C++ compilation locally and, with Horde, can distribute build actions across remote machines.
why: Reduces iteration time on large C++ codebases
Remote compilation can use otherwise idle machines
Especially useful once full editor builds become a productivity bottleneck
workflow: Measure local clean/incremental build times first.
For remote acceleration, configure Horde agents and secure access.
Track build reliability and speed before expanding the pool.
tools.codex: Codex can inspect BuildConfiguration and build logs, but should not alter distributed-build infrastructure without an explicit task.
tools.caution: Remote build support/platform details evolve by engine release; follow the exact UE 5.8 documentation and secure Horde authentication.

tools.title: Azure DevOps CI for Unreal
tools.priority: High when Azure hosts the game repo
tools.summary: Use an Azure Pipelines self-hosted build machine with Unreal installed to run validation, UBT/UAT, cook, package and test jobs.
why: Keeps the Unreal build environment under your control
Machine-level engine/cache state persists across jobs
Fits Azure Repos and branch policies
Can publish packaged builds/test artifacts automatically
workflow: Provision a dedicated self-hosted Windows agent with the exact Unreal version/toolchain.
Run lightweight validation first, then UBT/UAT build/cook/test stages.
Publish logs, test reports and packaged artifacts; gate protected branches on required jobs.
tools.codex: Codex can author/maintain azure-pipelines.yml and project build scripts, while engine credentials/signing secrets stay in secure variables.
tools.caution: Microsoft-hosted agents are usually a poor fit for large Unreal builds because the engine/toolchain/cache is heavy; prefer self-hosted agents for repeatable production builds.

tools.title: Multi-User Editing
tools.summary: Connects multiple Unreal Editor instances into a shared live editing session for real-time collaborative content work.
why: Multiple people can work together in the same world
Useful for review sessions, level dressing and collaborative iteration
Works on top of a defined source-control revision
workflow: Make every participant sync the exact same project revision and engine version.
Launch/join a short-lived Multi-User session on LAN/VPN.
At session end, persist and commit the agreed changes through normal source control.
tools.codex: Mostly a human collaboration tool; Codex should understand that the live session does not replace source control and should avoid conflicting automated writes during a session.
tools.caution: Epic explicitly positions Multi-User Editing as an addition to source control, not a replacement. Keep sessions short-lived and start from the same revision.

tools.title: One File Per Actor (OFPA)
tools.summary: Stores level Actor instance data in external files so different team members can modify different Actors without constantly touching the main level file.
why: Reduces source-control contention on large levels
Enabled by default with World Partition
Makes parallel world editing more practical
Cooked builds still embed Actors normally
workflow: Use World Partition or enable OFPA for the target level.
Keep actor edits scoped and review source-control changes carefully.
Use locks/source-control discipline for assets that remain indivisible.
Validate level load/cook after large structural changes.
tools.codex: When editing level actors, Codex should understand OFPA-generated files as engine-owned content and avoid renaming/manipulating them directly on disk.
tools.caution: OFPA helps actor-level contention but does not make arbitrary .uasset files mergeable.

tools.title: Unreal Collaboration Strategy: Git LFS + Locks + Short-Lived Branches
tools.summary: A practical team policy for binary Unreal content: LFS storage, explicit locks for non-mergeable assets, small branches and frequent synchronization.
why: Keeps binary history out of normal Git object storage
Makes ownership of currently edited assets visible
workflow: Track Unreal binary assets with Git LFS before adding them.
Lock high-conflict binary assets before editing.
Pull/rebase before starting significant asset work.
Keep branches/tasks narrow and integrate frequently.
Never resolve a binary merge by guessing; choose one asset revision or merge using Unreal-aware tooling when supported.
tools.codex: Before modifying binary assets, Codex should inspect source-control status/locks and avoid parallel edits to the same asset.
tools.caution: LFS does not make binary assets mergeable. Coordination and locking remain necessary.

tools.title: Gameplay Tags
tools.summary: Hierarchical identifiers for gameplay state, categories, abilities, effects and cross-system queries.
why: Works with GAS and other systems
workflow: Use tags for semantic state/categories, not arbitrary data.
Validate references and avoid near-duplicate meanings.
tools.codex: Prefer Gameplay Tags when multiple systems need a shared semantic vocabulary.
tools.caution: Tags can become an ungoverned global namespace; maintain conventions.

tools.title: Enhanced Input
tools.summary: Asset-based input actions, triggers, modifiers and mapping contexts for contextual/remappable controls.
workflow: Keep gameplay actions separate from physical keys.
tools.codex: Codex can create consistent input assets/handlers once corresponding MCP asset tools exist.
tools.caution: Avoid binding gameplay logic directly to raw keys throughout Blueprints.

tools.title: Common UI
tools.summary: Layered UI/input framework designed for complex game menus and multi-input navigation.
workflow: Integrate with the current UE 5.8 input model.
Test keyboard/gamepad focus and back/accept behavior.
tools.codex: Useful target architecture for menu-heavy games instead of ad-hoc widget creation/removal.
tools.caution: Adopt for real navigation complexity; simple HUD-only games may not need it.

tools.title: StateTree
tools.summary: Hierarchical state machine combining state-machine transitions with selector-style hierarchy.
workflow: Avoid replacing simple booleans with a StateTree unnecessarily.
tools.codex: Strong candidate for AI/NPC/interactable state systems; we should add dedicated read/write MCP support.
tools.caution: StateTree is an architecture choice, not a universal replacement for Behavior Trees or simple state variables.

tools.title: Gameplay Ability System (GAS)
tools.summary: Framework for abilities, attributes, effects, cues, costs, cooldowns, replication and prediction.
workflow: Put ASC ownership in the correct Actor/PlayerState.
tools.codex: When the game has substantial combat/abilities, prefer GAS over custom one-off cooldown/buff systems.
tools.caution: GAS has a learning/architecture cost; do not add it to a tiny prototype without need.

tools.title: Game Features / Modular Gameplay
tools.summary: Feature-plugin approach for modular gameplay content that can be activated/deactivated independently.
why: Useful for teams working on parallel game features
workflow: Keep a feature's content/code/data inside its feature plugin.
Use shared core modules only for stable contracts.
tools.codex: Good architecture when Codex is tasked with an isolated feature; boundaries make changes safer.
tools.caution: Adds project structure complexity; not required for every small game.

tools.title: Procedural Content Generation (PCG)
tools.summary: Node-based procedural content framework for scattering, generation and data-driven environment workflows.
workflow: Profile generated content and keep runtime/editor generation strategy explicit.
tools.codex: UE 5.8 includes PCG toolsets in the Toolset Registry family, making it a strong target for AI-assisted generation.
tools.caution: Procedural generation can hide performance/content explosion; set budgets and validate outputs.

tools.title: Mass Entity / Mass Framework
tools.summary: Data-oriented entity framework for large numbers of agents/entities and scalable simulation.
workflow: Use only when actor-per-entity architecture becomes a measured bottleneck.
tools.codex: Specialized architecture; Codex should not introduce Mass unless project scale warrants it.
tools.caution: Higher conceptual complexity than Actors/Components; premature adoption can slow development.

tools.title: Blueprint Architecture: Components, Interfaces, Dispatchers & Subsystems
tools.summary: Use composition and explicit contracts to prevent giant, tightly-coupled Blueprint classes.
workflow: Put reusable actor behavior in Actor Components.
Use Blueprint Interfaces for capability contracts.
Use Event Dispatchers for one-to-many notifications.
Keep widgets as presentation, not game-state owners.
tools.codex: Default architecture rules for generated Blueprint systems; refactor before graphs become giant.
tools.caution: Do not replace every direct reference with an interface/event; choose the simplest decoupling that fits ownership.

tools.title: C++ / Blueprint Boundary Strategy
tools.summary: Keep stable/high-performance/framework code in C++ and fast content/gameplay iteration in Blueprints.
workflow: Keep tuning/content assembly in Blueprint/Data Assets.
Move hotspots or fragile duplicated logic to C++ only when justified.
tools.codex: Codex should choose the lane deliberately instead of converting everything to C++ or leaving everything in Blueprint.
tools.caution: Avoid blueprint-only private engine reimplementations and avoid C++ for every tiny designer-tuned behavior.

tools.title: Naming & Folder Conventions
tools.summary: Consistent asset prefixes, feature folders and ownership boundaries make large Unreal projects searchable and automatable.
why: Codex can infer asset intent from names
workflow: Define prefixes for major asset types.
Avoid dumping assets into generic Misc folders.
tools.codex: Naming conventions directly improve agent search precision and reduce accidental edits.
tools.caution: Do not over-engineer names with excessive abbreviations; optimize for team comprehension and automation.

tools.title: Lyra Sample Game as Architecture Reference
tools.summary: Epic-maintained modular multiplayer sample demonstrating modern UE architecture including Game Features, GAS, Enhanced Input and scalable UI/gameplay patterns.
why: Real production-style examples instead of isolated snippets
Strong reference for multiplayer, abilities, inventory/equipment and UI architecture
workflow: Install the Lyra version matching the target engine.
Study one subsystem relevant to the current feature instead of copying the whole project.
Document the pattern and why it fits your game.
Implement a smaller project-specific version and validate complexity before expanding.
tools.codex: Codex can use Lyra as a pattern reference, but should not cargo-cult class names or architecture that the current game does not need.
tools.caution: Lyra is a learning/reference project, not a mandatory starter architecture; its complexity can be excessive for small games.

tools.title: Behavior Trees & Blackboards
tools.summary: Event-driven decision trees backed by Blackboard state for scalable NPC behavior.
workflow: Use Services sparingly for periodic updates.
Debug with the live Behavior Tree and Gameplay Debugger.
tools.codex: Codex can author Tasks/Services and review graph complexity; future MCP readers should expose tree nodes and Blackboard keys.
tools.caution: Do not turn the Blackboard into a global dumping ground or run expensive Services every tick.

tools.title: Environment Query System (EQS)
tools.summary: Scores generated locations or actors against tests so AI can choose cover, vantage points, pickups and other context-sensitive targets.
workflow: Create a focused query with a small candidate set.
Use EQS debugging visualization and profile expensive tests.
tools.codex: Useful for replacing hand-written nearest/cover search loops with an engine-native query asset.
tools.caution: Large generators and expensive traces can become a hidden AI performance cost.

tools.title: AI Perception
tools.summary: Sensory framework for sight, hearing, damage and custom stimuli that feeds AI awareness.
workflow: Add AI Perception to the controller.
Store semantic state rather than re-querying perception everywhere.
tools.codex: Codex should prefer perception events over ad-hoc distance checks on Tick for awareness systems.
tools.caution: Tune sight/hearing ranges and affiliation filters; uncontrolled perception across many agents can be expensive.

tools.title: Smart Objects
tools.summary: Reservation-based world interaction points that advertise activities to AI and players.
why: Decouples world interactions from specific NPC classes
Scales benches, doors, workstations and ambient behaviors
workflow: Release the slot reliably on completion/cancel.
tools.codex: Good architecture for systemic NPC/environment interactions instead of casts to every interactable class.
tools.caution: Always handle cancellation and reservation release; orphaned claims create hard-to-debug AI stalls.

tools.title: World Partition
tools.summary: Grid-based automatic level streaming and large-world data management with OFPA, Data Layers and builder commandlets.
workflow: Define streaming sources and data layers.
Use builder commandlets for batch work.
Profile streaming and memory on target hardware.
tools.codex: Codex can maintain world-partition config and invoke builder commandlets, but should not bulk-resave a world without a clean branch and validation.
tools.caution: Streaming grids and cross-cell references need architectural discipline; do not enable merely because the project uses UE5.

tools.title: World Partition HLOD
tools.summary: Generates proxy representations for unloaded World Partition cells to reduce draw calls while preserving distant scenery.
workflow: Create HLOD layers by content type.
Run full HLOD builder in CI/release pipelines.
Validate visual transitions and package size.
tools.codex: A strong candidate for project scripts that build only changed/target regions and report failures.
tools.caution: HLOD generation can create many binary changes; coordinate source control and avoid unnecessary full rebuilds.

tools.title: Rewind Debugger
tools.summary: Records PIE gameplay and lets developers scrub backward through animation/gameplay traces to inspect what actually happened.
workflow: Pause and select the target object.
tools.codex: Use trace findings as evidence when Codex edits animation logic instead of describing the bug from memory.
tools.caution: Enable Pose Watch/trace data intentionally; recording everything can add overhead and noise.

tools.title: Animation Insights
tools.summary: Unreal Insights extension for observing animation state, blend values and animation performance over recorded traces.
tools.codex: Provide Codex with the measured track/state evidence before refactoring complex animation systems.
tools.caution: Profile representative gameplay; editor preview behavior may not match a packaged target exactly.

tools.title: Control Rig
tools.summary: In-engine rigging and procedural animation framework usable from Sequencer, Animation Blueprints and gameplay Blueprints.
why: Rig and adjust characters without round-tripping every change to a DCC
Full Body IK and modular rig workflows
workflow: Create a Control Rig from the skeletal mesh.
Use it in Sequencer or Anim Blueprints where appropriate.
Use Rewind/Animation Insights for runtime diagnosis.
tools.codex: Useful target for future graph extraction/authoring support and for generating project-specific procedural rig utilities.
tools.caution: Separate rig authoring from gameplay state ownership; complex per-frame rigs can be costly.

tools.title: Motion Warping
tools.summary: Dynamically adjusts root motion to align animation windows with named world targets for mantling, melee, traversal and interactions.
why: Reuse animations across variable target positions
Avoids bespoke animations for every distance
workflow: Set/update named warp targets before playback.
Test edge distances/rotations and network behavior.
tools.codex: Codex can build consistent traversal/melee wrappers around warp targets instead of hard-coded teleport corrections.
tools.caution: Beta feature; validate root-motion, prediction and multiplayer behavior on the exact target engine/build.

tools.title: Motion Matching / Pose Search
tools.summary: Query-driven pose selection from animation databases as an alternative to large hand-authored locomotion state machines.
why: Scales by adding quality animation data
workflow: Define a schema and pose database.
Tune cost weights with representative gameplay.
Profile database/query cost and debug selections.
tools.codex: Use as a deliberate animation architecture, not an automatic replacement for every state machine.
tools.caution: Quality depends heavily on animation coverage/data preparation; a sparse database will not be rescued by code.

tools.title: Niagara VFX
tools.summary: Unreal's modern programmable VFX system for reusable CPU/GPU particle and simulation effects.
workflow: Build reusable modules before giant one-off graphs.
Expose user parameters for gameplay control.
Profile with Niagara Debugger on target scenarios.
tools.codex: Node2Code can help with read context today; future native MCP tools should inspect/author Niagara graphs directly.
tools.caution: VFX can silently consume GPU/CPU/memory; define effect budgets and scalability levels early.

tools.title: Niagara Debugger
tools.summary: Live level-wide inspection and performance analysis for Niagara systems, emitters and parameters.
why: Faster VFX debugging than graph inspection alone
tools.codex: Use debugger output as objective evidence before asking Codex to optimize Niagara content.
tools.caution: Optimize representative scenes; isolated editor previews can hide aggregate VFX cost.

tools.title: MetaSounds
tools.summary: Sample-accurate DSP graph system for procedural, interactive and reusable audio sources.
why: Procedural audio without external middleware for many cases
workflow: Create reusable Patches for shared DSP logic.
Profile render cost and voice counts.
Keep gameplay events and audio rendering responsibilities separate.
tools.codex: Strong future MCP graph target; today Codex can help design parameter contracts and Builder API utilities.
tools.caution: Audio graphs are DSP flow graphs, not Blueprint execution graphs; reason about real-time audio constraints.

tools.title: MetaSound Builder API
tools.summary: Blueprint/C++ API for procedurally creating and modifying MetaSound Sources/Patches and graph connections.
why: Can create assets from Editor Utility Blueprints
Excellent candidate for Codex-native audio tooling
workflow: Use the Builder subsystem for in-memory/runtime generation.
Use the Editor subsystem for asset authoring.
Wrap repetitive project patterns in deterministic helpers.
Verify documented unsupported graph features before relying on them.
tools.codex: This is the preferred engine-native foundation for future MetaSound MCP tools instead of UI automation.
tools.caution: The API is Beta and has documented limitations; pin to UE 5.8 and smoke-test after engine upgrades.

tools.title: RenderDoc Integration
tools.summary: Single-frame GPU graphics capture integrated into Unreal for inspecting draw events, resources, pipeline state and shaders.
workflow: Install RenderDoc and enable/attach the Unreal plugin.
Fix and capture the same scenario again.
tools.codex: Provide capture findings/event names to Codex for targeted rendering changes; do not ask it to optimize blindly from FPS alone.
tools.caution: Full-resource/callstack captures can become very large and profiling itself adds overhead.

tools.title: Render Resource Viewer
tools.summary: Snapshot of GPU memory allocations with resource size, flags, owner asset and filtering/search.
workflow: Open the viewer in the representative scene.
Browse large allocations to the owning asset.
tools.codex: Future MCP export could rank resource owners automatically; for now use the viewer to supply measured asset targets.
tools.caution: It is a snapshot, not continuous tracing; refresh after state changes.

tools.title: Iris Replication System
tools.summary: Opt-in next-generation replication system designed for larger worlds/player counts with shared work, filtering and prioritization.
why: Existing replicated properties/RPCs remain largely compatible
workflow: First build correct authoritative gameplay with normal replication.
Evaluate Iris on a dedicated branch.
tools.codex: Codex must not flip a project to Iris as a casual optimization; migration needs architecture review and measured validation.
tools.caution: Epic marks Iris Experimental in UE 5.8; use caution for shipping and verify all project-specific replication behaviors.

tools.title: Replication Graph
tools.summary: Persistent replication-list graph that scales server relevancy work for large numbers of Actors and clients.
why: Good bridge when generic replication becomes CPU-bound
workflow: Create focused custom nodes only where needed.
tools.codex: Use only after profiling shows replication-list generation is a bottleneck; Codex can help implement/test custom nodes.
tools.caution: Adds networking architecture complexity and the plugin is marked Beta; splitscreen limitations are documented.

tools.title: Crash Reporter + Crash Context
tools.summary: Captures crash IDs, call stacks, logs, system data and custom game context, with support for routing packaged-game reports to your own backend/service.
workflow: Include Crash Reporter in test/release packages.
Route reports to an approved service/backend.
Add compact custom context such as map/mode/build/session.
Triage recurring signatures and link fixes to build versions.
tools.codex: Codex can analyze symbolicated call stacks/logs and correlate them with source changes; never send secrets/PII as crash context.
tools.caution: Packaged builds need explicit Crash Reporter configuration; protect user privacy and keep symbols/build IDs organized.

tools.title: Structured Unreal Logging Strategy
tools.summary: Use project-specific log categories, appropriate verbosity and structured UE_LOGFMT messages so bugs are searchable instead of buried in LogTemp spam.
why: Structured fields are easier for Codex to interpret
workflow: Create one category per meaningful subsystem/domain.
Use Error/Warning only for actionable problems.
Use Log/Verbose for normal diagnostic detail.
Prefer UE_LOGFMT for structured messages where useful.
Allow verbosity overrides via -LogCmds during debugging.
tools.codex: Logs should include stable identifiers/state needed for diagnosis; Codex can then search logs deterministically without parsing arbitrary on-screen text.
tools.caution: Never log secrets/tokens/PII, and avoid per-frame spam in normal verbosity levels.
